clue.text: Sign of injury at the start of a run

indicators.note: being at the start of something places the first piece in front of the one that follows

parts.note: a scar is the mark a healed wound leaves
'a' as in 'five pounds a head' means per

explanation.surface: A runner picks up a visible wound right at the start of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' must be read as PER, the sense in 'twice a day'. Scarper is informal British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is British slang for fleeing or bolting, which is to run off quickly.

clue.text: Bird on board ship moves quickly

indicators.note: something on board a vessel is carried inside it, so the bird goes within the ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation for a ship
a coot is a black water bird

explanation.surface: A bird aboard a ship darts about.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoot is to go somewhere fast or dash off, an informal verb for hurrying.

clue.text: A jolly lot facing endless sorrow in a sort of depression

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
facing something means standing in front of it, so these pieces come first

parts.note: taken as written
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, so the whole lot is the Royal Marines, RM
pity is sorrow felt for another

explanation.surface: A cheerful crowd meets a gloomy person sunk in depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood; here it is a hollow in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is the hollow under the arm where it joins the shoulder, a physical dip in the body's surface.

clue.text: Rescue pets suffering tortures

indicators.note: something suffering is damaged and knocked out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: both words taken as written, as ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Rescued pets that have suffered cruelty, as at an animal shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To persecute is to harass or ill-treat someone cruelly and persistently, so it is a synonym of torment or torture.

clue.text: Disprove underground stem can shoot up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means read from bottom to top, the wrong way

parts.note: a tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen underground stem

explanation.surface: A botanist argues that a plant's underground stem can sprout upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks botanical, matching the stem; it is the instruction to go up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute an argument or claim by offering evidence against it, so it means to prove false.

clue.text: Be defeated in sporting contest, showing clip of film?

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it, so the defeat goes within the contest

parts.note: a cup is a knockout sporting competition
to lose is to be defeated

explanation.surface: A team that loses a match has its embarrassing moment replayed on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a single shot filmed at very short range, a fragment of footage; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Timidity of animal on something slippery crossing a road

indicators.note: crossing something means straddling it, so the two outer pieces sit either side of it
one thing on another sits beside it, so the animal comes before the next piece

parts.note: a cow is a farm animal
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road
ice is notoriously slippery

explanation.surface: A nervous cow hesitates before crossing an icy road.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardice is lack of courage in the face of danger, the same timorous quality as timidity.

clue.text: Food no good for ibexes etc.

indicators.note: with no good means with the letter for good taken away

parts.note: ibexes are wild mountain goats
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A feed that is unsuitable for ibexes and similar animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good for' reads as a verdict on the food; it is the deletion plus a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grain eaten as porridge or fed to horses, so they are a kind of foodstuff.

clue.text: Spiritual home ultimately found at that place with a lake

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
there means at that place
the 'a' taken as written, 'with' joining it on
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A spiritual retreat is finally discovered beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal describes something delicate and otherworldly, heavenly rather than earthly, which is close to spiritual.

clue.text: Use material to protect plants in small fields

parts.note: to pad is to cushion something with material
docks are broad-leaved weeds

explanation.surface: A gardener wraps plants in fabric to shield them in small enclosures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like the thing protected; it supplies the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddock is a small enclosed field, usually beside stables, where horses are kept or exercised.

clue.text: Shell men found by French sea

indicators.note: standing by something means standing next to it, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: Seashells collected by men on a French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an edible abalone found around the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is a sea snail whose ear-shaped shell is lined with mother-of-pearl, so a shell creature names it.

clue.text: Mesmerized, we turned round with irritating pain in bed

indicators.note: being in something means held inside it, so the bed wraps round the rest

parts.note: taken as written; it splits around the other pieces

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the other way, so the word we is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
an itch is an irritating sensation

explanation.surface: Someone lies in bed tossing and turning, troubled by an itch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be bewitched is to be held under a spell, entranced or captivated, which is what mesmerized means.

clue.text: Tries somehow to get involved with terms — US terms?

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified manner, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the first of the two appearances, taken as written as the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone tries to engage with the terms of a deal, then notices Americans use different words.
explanation.walkthrough: Many American colleges divide the year into trimesters where British ones have terms, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three divisions of an academic year in some American schools, the equivalent of a British school term.

clue.text: Jumper found in bedroom

indicators.note: something found in a word is sitting inside its spelling, waiting to be picked out

parts.note: the middle three letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sweater has turned up in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater, which suits a bedroom; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A roo, short for kangaroo, is an Australian marsupial that moves by hopping on powerful back legs.

clue.text: Report line being tampered with — someone invading privacy

indicators.note: something tampered with has been meddled with and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written, as ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A phone line has been bugged by a snooper eavesdropping on calls.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is an intruder who pushes in where they are not wanted, meddling in other people's affairs.

clue.text: Quiet son, moved by account of Jesus's life?

indicators.note: standing by means next to, so one piece sits alongside the other
letters that are moved shift out of their places into a new order

parts.note: both words taken as written, as eight letters of fodder
Mark's Gospel is one of the four accounts of Jesus's life

explanation.surface: A quiet son is moved to tears by reading the Gospel story.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation mark itself, the '?' closing the clue, which looks like a mere hint of whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol printed at the end of the clue is the very punctuation sign used to end an interrogative sentence.

clue.text: Group gathering around heretic may be such

definitions.text: Group gathering around heretic may be such

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
an Arian follows Arius, whose view of Christ was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A faction that rallies round a dissenting preacher could be called this.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a religious group clustering round a heretic is sectarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian means belonging to or bigoted on behalf of a sect, the outlook of a splinter religious faction.

clue.text: Amidst stress, I had twist of fate

indicators.note: being amidst something means in the middle of it, so this piece goes inside

parts.note: accent is stress placed on a syllable
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Under pressure, someone suffers a sudden turn of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had' belongs with 'I' in the wordplay as well as reading on: 'I had' is shortened to I'd.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned chance event, often unlucky, which is what a twist of fate means.

clue.text: Fish only some fishermen had enjoyed

indicators.note: only some of the words is used, a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Only a few anglers had a good day's catch.
explanation.definitionFit: The menhaden is an oily North Atlantic fish of the herring family, caught for fishmeal and oil.

clue.text: Artful idiot thrown out of form always, not just once

indicators.note: doing something not just once means doing it again, so the whole piece is written twice
someone thrown out of a place is removed from it, so the idiot leaves the form

parts.note: a form is a school class
an ass is a fool
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A sly fool is expelled from his school class, and not for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is the British name for a school year group or class.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever-clever describes someone too keen to look smart, showy and cunning, which is a sense of artful.

clue.text: Individual record

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a release of one song

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a personal best or one person's file; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sole or one-person as an adjective and, as a noun, a short release carrying one main track.

clue.text: American following food channel

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so this piece goes second

parts.note: meat is food, as in 'meat and drink'
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American viewer tunes in to a cookery TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests television; it is an anatomical passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatus is an anatomical passage or opening in the body, such as the duct of the ear.

clue.text: One with quiet word expressing some reservation?

indicators.note: one thing with another means the two go together, placed side by side

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sh is the sound made to call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs a hesitant word quietly, not fully committing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ish, used on its own, is informal shorthand for 'sort of' or 'more or less', a hedge on what was just said.

clue.text: Being terribly blue, I read a poet

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched and disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling miserable, someone reads a gloomy poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The melancholy surface suits the poet, whose Les Fleurs du mal is famously bleak.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Baudelaire was the nineteenth-century French writer of Les Fleurs du mal, a celebrated verse collection.

clue.text: Daughter and little brother, primarily seen as nerd

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
wee is Scottish and informal for small

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A girl and her small brother are mainly regarded as geeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a socially awkward, boring or studious person, much like a geek.

clue.text: Some land that is holy, without beginning or end

indicators.note: lacking a beginning and an end means the first and last letters are cut away

parts.note: sacred means holy

explanation.surface: A plot of land is sacred, eternal, with no beginning or end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without beginning or end' sounds like a description of the divine, matching 'holy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres, so it is a measured amount of ground.

clue.text: English square occupied by GP right about glands and hormones etc.

indicators.note: a space occupied by people has them inside it, so the doctor and right go within the square

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
nine is a square number, three times three
a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A British doctor's square-shaped note sets out facts about glands and hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a shape or a plaza; it is a square number. A GP is a family doctor in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocrine system is the network of ductless glands secreting hormones into the blood, so the word covers that whole area.

clue.text: Greek character, contemptible person to live in squalor

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
git is British slang for a nasty or stupid person

explanation.surface: A disreputable Greek fellow chooses to live in filth.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig it is an informal idiom meaning to live in dirty, untidy, crowded conditions, like animals in a sty.

clue.text: Can bird appear in Welsh village?

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a bird might turn up in a Welsh village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a verb asking permission; it is the noun, a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintern is a village in Monmouthshire, Wales, on the River Wye, famous for its ruined Cistercian abbey.

clue.text: People in charge of boats keep out birds almost entirely

indicators.note: almost entirely means all but a little, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to bar is to keep out or exclude
geese are birds

explanation.surface: Boat crews try to keep birds away from their vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: A bargee is the British word for someone who works a canal barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bargees are the crew or skippers who operate barges on canals and rivers, the boatmen in charge.
